solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bizarre eponym worked for lad on warship

indicators.note: bizarre suggests something weird and twisted, so the letters of the next two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: An oddly named eponym somehow got a job aboard a naval vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' reads as a verb about the eponym but is simply part of the letters to rearrange along with EPONYM.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a boy employed on a warship to carry gunpowder from the magazine to the guns.

clue.text: Not complete in showing bias

explanation.surface: Something incomplete that is also prejudiced.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both incomplete (a part-only result) and prejudiced in favour of one side.

clue.text: Reception FT compilers attend, consuming litres

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing up, so the litre abbreviation goes inside the pair of words

parts.note: the setters of the Financial Times puzzles speak of themselves as we
to attend a party is to come to it

explanation.surface: The FT's crossword setters turn up at a reception and down plenty of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A reception is the greeting a guest receives on arrival, a synonym in noun form.

clue.text: Mysterious magnetic variation around island

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap round the island abbreviation
a variation is a changed version, so the letters of magnetic are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzling shift in the magnetic field is detected around some island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation' rearranges MAGNETIC, and 'around' puts that jumble round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something baffling and hard to interpret is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Oil sprinkled on second radish

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a second

indicators.note: sprinkled suggests drops scattered about, so the letters of oil are mixed up

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction: drizzle oil onto a second radish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' looks like a second radish but is the short word for a moment; 'sprinkled' rearranges the oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A long white East Asian variety of radish, also called daikon, is an example of the category.

clue.text: Necessary end with fuel exploding

indicators.note: something exploding is blown apart, so the letters of end and fuel are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: An unavoidable finish involving fuel blowing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Required or essential is the old-fashioned sense of the word, a synonym of necessary.

clue.text: Saying sliced pie good with butter

indicators.note: a pie that is sliced is cut up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ram is something that butts, a butter in the crossword sense

explanation.surface: A recipe: cut a pie, add something good, serve with butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sliced' rearranges PIE to EPI; 'butter' is not the spread but one who butts.
explanation.definitionFit: A witty, pithy remark is a kind of saying, a near-synonym.

clue.text: Make one joyous sound about another killing

indicators.note: about says the first sound goes round the second one

parts.note: singing is making a joyful sound
another joyous sound, laughter

explanation.surface: A paradox: one cheerful noise wrapped around another adds up to murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' carries over 'joyous sound' from the first phrase, so two different happy noises are needed, one wrapping the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Massacring or butchering in large numbers is a synonym for killing, used as a noun.

clue.text: German rock singer teaching the French one

parts.note: lore is traditional teaching or knowledge
le is French for the
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A German rock vocalist giving lessons to a French one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock singer' suggests a band musician; here it is a siren sitting on a rock above the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: In German legend, a siren on a cliff by the Rhine whose song lured boatmen to their deaths.

clue.text: Girl is delayed coming to king's monument

indicators.note: delayed means the word is comes later, moved from the front of the name to its end

parts.note: Isobel is a girl's name
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A girl turns up late at the king's monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is delayed' takes the IS at the start of ISOBEL and moves it to the back, giving OBELIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tapering stone pillar is a classic kind of monument.

clue.text: Campanologists should be up to speed

definitions.text: Campanologists should be up to speed

parts.words: Campanologists should be up to speed
parts.note: bell-ringers pull ropes, and being familiar with the ropes is an idiom for being experienced

explanation.surface: Bell-ringers ought to be fully trained.
explanation.walkthrough: Campanologists are bell-ringers, who literally handle ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being familiar with how things are done, read literally for bell-ringers.

clue.text: Regular college class

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
a form is a class in a British school

explanation.surface: A routine university lecture group.
explanation.walkthrough: A FORM is a school class in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means unvarying or consistent, a synonym of regular.

clue.text: Fail to draw positive conclusion in Dante's work?

definitions.text: Fail to draw positive conclusion in Dante's work?

parts.words: Fail to draw positive conclusion in Dante's work?
parts.note: to ... is to conclude the negative, and split that way it names the first part of Dante's Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A critic finds nothing good to say about a poem by Dante.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as INFER NO: to deduce 'no', which is failing to reach a positive conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: The first part of the Divine Comedy, describing hell, is Dante's work.

clue.text: Share hole where fool accommodates fifty

indicators.note: accommodates means takes in, so the fifty numeral goes inside the word for fool

parts.note: to have someone is to fool them
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A golfer's joke on the green where a clown has taken fifty shots.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, two players who take the same score on a hole are said to share it, using this word.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, to tie a hole with an opponent by taking the same number of strokes.

clue.text: Spell-check?

parts.note: a spell is a period of time, and a check on it is a cap on its length

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks like spelling words; it means a stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadline or maximum duration restrains a spell of time, a cryptic reading of a computing term.

clue.text: Meat cut from prize animal

parts.note: a medal is a prize
a lion is an animal

explanation.surface: A butcher takes meat from a show-winning beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round slice of meat, such as of beef or pork, is a cut.

clue.text: Transported via Gate 4?

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Passengers are carried through Gate 4 at an airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transported' suggests travel, but it means delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carried away with delight or enchanted is the figurative sense of transported.

clue.text: Mediterranean metropolis has a live TV broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaside city puts out a live television programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city of Israel, on its Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: American with risk to run as accomplice

parts.note: to bet is to risk money
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An American gambler running off as somebody's partner in crime.
explanation.definitionFit: One who helps or encourages another in wrongdoing is a synonym for accomplice.

clue.text: Take action to receive credit in Bolivian city

indicators.note: to receive means to take in, so the credit abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: Someone goes to court to be paid what is owed in a Bolivian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The constitutional capital of Bolivia, a city in the south of the country.

clue.text: Endless fuss in the main poetic structure

indicators.note: in says the trimmed word is placed inside the sea word

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the sea

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to raise a stink is to make a fuss

explanation.surface: A ceaseless commotion at sea set out in verse form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the last letter of the fuss word; 'the main' is an old poetic name for the open ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: An intricate verse form of six six-line stanzas plus an envoi, with recurring end-words.

clue.text: Platform elevated with two-way struts?

parts.note: a raised runway where models strut up and down, out and back

explanation.surface: A raised platform held up by struts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struts' looks like supporting beams, but it is what models do walking both ways along the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised narrow stage on which fashion models parade, walking to the end and back.

clue.text: Complaint setter will put to head

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I, so setter will is I'll
a ness is a headland, a head of land

explanation.surface: A crossword setter plans to put a grievance to the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not a boss but a headland, NESS, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an ailment or sickness.

clue.text: Pressing need perhaps to have small animals harnessed

parts.note: a team is a group of animals harnessed together, such as oxen

explanation.surface: An urgent requirement to put small animals in harness.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing, or pressing clothes, often uses vapour from the iron, so it is an example of what pressing needs.

clue.text: Aristotle so thought to contain kingdom

indicators.note: to contain says the answer sits within the run of letters

explanation.surface: The philosopher believed something would hold a kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mountain monarchy in southern Africa, surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Yielded to pressure about wildly excessive dance

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for yielded wraps round the abbreviation

parts.note: to give is to yield under pressure
OTT is short for over the top

explanation.surface: Someone caves in and dances with wild abandon.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT, over the top, is British shorthand for excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: An old French folk dance in moderate four-time, an example of a dance.

clue.text: Mock one worried about educational establishment

indicators.note: about says the pair of words goes round the institution

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
ate is used of a worry, as in what's eating you
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone anxious about a school is ridiculed.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock is to ape or mimic, a synonym verb.

clue.text: All-male hike excluding absolutely no-one?

parts.note: all means every
a man is a male
to jack up prices is to hike them

explanation.surface: A men-only walk which nonetheless leaves nobody out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hike' suggests a walk; here it is a raise, as in jack up.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning each and every person, so leaving out nobody at all.
